I am 68 years old and have farmed these lands for 45 years. My 14 mu are all in wheat-maize rotation — I know every plot by heart. I have a well for irrigation, and my household has three people to help with the busy seasons. I did not go to school for long, but I have learned what works from decades of working this soil.

For wheat, I will rotary till the fields in October and sow improved wheat seeds — the reliable varieties I have used for years, about 15 kg per mu. I will put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea when the wheat turns green in spring. I will irrigate four times from my well: once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once when the wheat revives in March, once at jointing, and once at heading. I will spray herbicide and insecticide four times in total to keep weeds and aphids under control. If the weather treats me fairly, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For maize, there is no time to waste after wheat harvest in early June. I will plant hybrid maize seeds directly into the stubble without tillage — everyone here does it this way now. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice: once after sowing if the soil is dry, and again at flowering. I will spray pesticides three times for weeds and corn borers. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
